senses.definition: Situated in, designed to be used in, or carried on in the open air.

quotes.text: A very neat old woman, still in her good outdoor coat and best beehive hat, was sitting at a polished mahogany table on whose surface there were several scored scratches so deep that a triangular piece of the veneer had come cleanly away,[…].
quotes.reference: 1963, Margery Allingham, “Foreword”, in The China Governess: A Mystery, London: Chatto & Windus, →OCLC:

senses.definition: Pertaining to charity administered or received away from, or independently from, a workhouse or other institution.

quotes.text: Believing social policy should be directed by experts to bring about the greatest happiness of the greatest number, Benthamites judged the old Poor Law outdoor relief system a recipe for waste and idleness.
quotes.reference: 1997, Roy Porter, The Greatest Benefit to Mankind, Folio Society, published 2016, page 395:
